whatIsPto.question: What is PTO?
whatIsPto.answer: PTO stands for Paid Time Off: the number of paid days off your employer gives you each year to use however you want. Unlike sick leave or public holidays, PTO days are yours to schedule freely. Most people take them at random and get less rest out of them than they could. Forever PTO helps you place those days strategically around public holidays to turn, say, 5 PTO days into 12 consecutive days off.

whatIs.question: What is this?
whatIs.answer: Forever PTO suggests which days to request off, based on the public holidays and your preferences. You can choose different strategies to spread time off across the year, customize holiday names, and add company-specific or regional holidays.

whyNotSeeingCountry.question: Why am I not seeing my country or holidays correctly?
whyNotSeeingCountry.answer: For simplicity and performance we use a third-party tool to get the public holidays for a given country and year. It may happen that your country or region is not supported or the data is not up to date. To fix this you can add custom holidays specific to your needs.

pricing.question: Why is there a paid model?
pricing.answer: Forever PTO is free to use. The paid model covers data and hosting, and pays for updates and support. The core features stay free.

premium.question: What does premium unlock?
premium.answer: Premium unlocks the planner's advanced controls: editing the suggested days by hand, adding your own holidays, planning past days, carry-over months into the next year, the advanced metrics and charts, and exporting your plan to your calendar. Planning with any strategy, country and region stays free.

carryOver.question: What are carry-over months?
carryOver.answer: If your company lets you use this year's PTO days in the first months of next year, carry-over months extend the planning window up to {max, number} months past December, so the planner can also place days in, say, January or February of the following year.

algorithms.question: How does the suggestion algorithm work?
algorithms.answer: The system looks at your available workdays, holidays and preferences (like skipping past dates) and finds every possible bridge, up to a whole working week. It then builds your plan one bridge at a time, always taking the one that adds the most new days off to what the plan already covers, under the rules of your strategy, so a weekend two bridges share is never counted twice.

strategies.question: What is the difference between the "grouped", "optimized", "balanced" and "main vacation" strategies?
strategies.answer: Optimized gets you the most effective days off per PTO day, mostly as long weekends spread across the year. Grouped trades some of that efficiency for a few long vacations of about two weeks. Balanced places a long weekend every few weeks, so you never go too long without a break. Main vacation puts one block of up to two weeks in the months you choose, then spends the rest like Optimized.

weekends.question: Do weekends and public holidays use up my PTO days?
weekends.answer: No. PTO days are only placed on workdays. Weekends and public holidays are already free, and that is exactly what the planner uses to stretch each PTO day into more days off.

alternatives.question: What are the alternatives?
alternatives.answer: Besides the suggestion, the planner builds other plans with the same budget, from your strategy and from the others, so you can compare how many days off each one gets you and apply the one you prefer with a click.

results.question: Why do recommendations change when I update preferences or holidays?
results.answer: Suggestions are recalculated in real time whenever your PTO budget, year, holidays, or strategy changes. Even small tweaks can reshuffle the rankings because the engine re-scores every possible bridge and block.

export.question: Can I add my plan to my calendar?
export.answer: Yes. With premium you can export your PTO days, the public holidays or both as an .ics file that works with Google Calendar, Apple Calendar, Outlook and any other calendar app, or as a PDF to print or share.

data.question: How do you handle my data?
data.answer: We store only the minimum information required to generate suggestions. We do not share data with third parties without consent. See the <privacyLink>privacy policy</privacyLink> for full details.

encryption.question: Is my data encrypted?
encryption.answer: Everything is stored locally in your browser: PTO days, selected dates, custom holidays, preferences. We apply light obfuscation so the data isn't readable at a glance, but the real protection is that we never send it to our servers.

tracking.question: Do you sell my data or track my vacation plans?
tracking.answer: No. Your planning data stays in your browser and is not sold to advertisers or data brokers. If analytics are enabled, they are limited to product measurement and never used to profile your vacation plans.

devices.question: Do I need an account? Can I use my plan on another device?
devices.answer: There are no accounts. Your plan lives in this browser, so another device or browser starts from scratch. Premium is tied to the email you donated with: on a new device, enter it in the premium window and access comes back.

code.question: How to contribute code or ideas?
code.answer: <link>Open issues or pull requests</link> with proposals. We need help on algorithms, integrations and UX improvements.

business.question: Propose integrations or corporate partnerships
business.answer: If you represent a company and want to integrate Forever PTO, reach out directly or open a GitHub issue with your proposal.

nonCode.question: Can I collaborate if I'm not a developer?
nonCode.answer: Yes. Feedback on UX, copy, translations, holiday accuracy, testing, and ideas is always useful. If you spot friction or have a specific need, just reach out.
